content: Printed QR codes fail on physical, not logical, grounds, and the print spec is part of the product. Documented thresholds: minimum printed width 2x2cm (below that, module edges land inside ordinary print tolerance); roughly 1cm of code width per 10cm of reading distance (a poster read from 3m needs about 30cm); printed modules at least 0.4mm on coated stock and 0.5mm on uncoated; quiet zone of exactly 4 modules on all four sides (ISO/IEC 18004); contrast around 7:1 for print versus 4:1 on screen, because print spends contrast on ink spread, paper reflectance and glare; error correction level M (~15% recovery) is the print default, Q (25%) for any print without a logo, H (30%) only with a centre logo or heavy handling. Raster exports need 300 DPI at final size with a whole number of pixels per module so no module edge is anti-aliased mid-pixel; vector (SVG/PDF) is what a print shop wants. Critically, raising error correction does NOT rescue a weak design: a controlled 48-colour-pair test found L->H made codes slightly worse on average, because the extra error-correction data makes the symbol denser, so each module is smaller and more fragile - error correction fixes damage covering part of a code (a logo), and is close to useless against damage spread evenly over the whole code (poor contrast, bad camera). Light-on-dark codes are a gamble: OpenCV read 40/40 dark-on-light but 0/8 light-on-dark, because ZXing tries both polarities and OpenCV does not - so dark modules on a light background is the only safe choice for codes you cannot control. Physical placement failures documented for wayfinding signage: steep viewing angle (foreshortening compresses modules), foot-traffic abrasion, anti-slip texture scattering light and blurring module edges, overhead glare on glossy floors, and the code being at the wrong height. Failure mode is easiest to avoid by designing for it: matte overlaminate, opaque light backer, larger codes so partial glare still leaves enough modules to finish the decode, complementary eye-level signs where glare is chronic, and a proof at final size on the real stock scanned with two different phones in the light the code will live in.
